name: Alvin Lucier
bio: American composer (1931–2021) whose works explore acoustic phenomena, resonance and the physics of sound. Best known for I Am Sitting in a Room (1969), where a recorded voice is replayed into a room until the room itself becomes the instrument.

name: Pauline Oliveros
bio: American composer and accordionist (1932–2016) who developed Deep Listening, a practice built around attentive, expanded listening to the sounds around us. A good starting point for anyone interested in listening as an artistic act.

name: Max Neuhaus
bio: Percussionist turned sound artist (1939–2009) who pioneered permanent sound installations in public space, including a long-running work beneath Times Square in New York.

name: Hugh Davies
bio: British electronic-music pioneer and instrument inventor (1943–2005), known for self-built electro-acoustic instruments made from found objects and contact-miked materials.

name: Harry Partch
bio: American composer (1901–1974) who designed and built his own instruments to play music in microtonal tunings, and wrote about his approach in Genesis of a Music.

name: Trimpin
bio: German-born, Seattle-based sound sculptor and inventor, known for kinetic, computer-controlled instruments and large-scale musical installations.

name: Christina Kubisch
bio: German sound artist known for her Electrical Walks, where specially built induction headphones reveal the hidden electromagnetic fields of cities and buildings.

name: Bill Fontana
bio: American sound artist known for sound sculptures that transplant live sounds from one place into another, often in public and architectural spaces.

name: Janet Cardiff & George Bures Miller
bio: Artist duo known for immersive sound installations and audio walks, including Forty Part Motet (2001), in which forty speakers each play one singer's voice.

name: Tristan Perich
bio: Composer and artist whose 1-bit electronic music is generated by a circuit on a chip, and who also makes large-scale installation and drawing machine works.

name: Nicolas Collins
bio: Composer, performer and author of Handmade Electronic Music, a hands-on guide to circuit bending and hardware hacking that has introduced a generation of makers to building their own sound circuits.

name: Laetitia Sonami
bio: Sound artist and performer who developed the Lady's Glove, a sensor-based instrument that lets her shape electronic sound through hand and finger movements.

name: Tod Machover
bio: Composer and MIT Media Lab professor who pioneered hyperinstruments — instruments enhanced with sensing and computation to extend what players can express.

name: Yuri Suzuki
bio: Sound artist and designer based in London, working across installations, instruments and products that make sound and music more tangible and playful.

name: Di Mainstone
bio: London-based artist and designer who creates wearable instruments and interactive sculptures, including the Human Harp, which turns the cables of bridges into playable strings.

name: Mi.Mu Gloves
bio: Wearable gestural instrument developed with musician Imogen Heap and a team of makers, letting performers control sound and music through movement of the hands.

name: Atau Tanaka
bio: Artist and researcher working on gestural musical interaction and bio-sensing, including performances using muscle sensors as an instrument. Based at Goldsmiths, University of London.

name: Rebecca Fiebrink
bio: Computer scientist and educator who created Wekinator, free software that lets artists and musicians build interactive systems by demonstrating examples to a machine learning model rather than writing code.

name: Ryoji Ikeda
bio: Japanese artist working with sound, light and data, known for large-scale audiovisual installations built from extremely precise electronic sound.
